A town councillor has told a debate how his elderly mother was "caught short" because of a lack of public toilets in Scarborough.
Reform UK councillor Robert Everall said his 87-year-old mother had visited her "favourite town one last time" but her "lasting memory of Scarborough is of having to go into Boyes to buy dry pads and underwear".
He was speaking in support of a motion for publicly-accessible loos in the redeveloped Brunswick Centre site.
The shopping centre closed in September 2025, but a recent council report said its public toilets would not be replaced in the redeveloped site, with facilities intended for customers.
The redeveloped centre, renamed as SQ1, is due to open in 2029 and is due to including a six-screen cinema, family leisure attraction, restaurants and shops.
Proposing the motion at Tuesday's meeting, town mayor Thomas Murray said some visitors were "reconsidering whether to come to the town because they can't be sure they'll find a toilet".
"For a family who needs a Changing Places facility, that can decide whether they come at all," said the Reform councillor.
A Changing Places toilet is a larger, specially equipped toilet designed for people with severe or multiple disabilities who cannot use standard accessible toilets.
Other councillors highlighted concerns about accessibility and the impact on local trade.
Some said they had been told by businesses that people were avoiding visiting the town centre because of a shortage of loos.
Earlier this month, Scarborough and Whitby Labour MP Alison Hume said residents were "sick of not having any public toilets".
The motion, unanimously approved on Tuesday, called for publicly-accessible toilets including accessible and Changing Places facilities to be included in SQ1, according to the Local Democracy Reporting Service.
It also asked North Yorkshire Council, the York and North Yorkshire Combined Authority and developers Scarborough Group International why public toilet provision was removed from earlier iterations of the scheme and how it could be reinstated.
